name: CUDA MPS provides no error isolation - one client crash kills all clients on the GPU
symptom: One inference engine crashes, and all other engines on the same GPU crash with it. The failure is not contained.
root_cause: CUDA MPS (Multi-Process Service) allows multiple processes to share a GPU, but they share the same GPU context. If one process triggers a CUDA error (OOM, illegal memory access), the error propagates to all processes sharing the GPU. MPS provides compute isolation (SM partitioning) but not error isolation.
workaround: Use MIG instead of MPS if error isolation is required. MIG provides hardware-level isolation including separate memory and compute contexts. Alternatively, run each inference engine in a separate container with its own GPU (no sharing). For development/testing, MPS is fine; for production multi-tenant serving, MIG or separate GPUs are safer.
notes: MPS is the simplest way to share a GPU across multiple inference engines, but it comes with a significant caveat: no error isolation. A single crash takes down all engines on the GPU. This is acceptable for development and testing, but for production multi-tenant serving, MIG or separate GPUs are safer. The tradeoff is that MIG has its own limitations (no NCCL support, shared NVLink bandwidth).
